title: Students from Lower-income Households Who Have Secured School Places through DSA and Assessment of Policy Impact
what_it_is: Students from Lower-income Households Who Have Secured School Places through DSA and Assessment of Policy Impact

sections.label: DSA scheme review and access
sections.summary: About 6% of DSA students were on financial aid over five years, and MOE is reviewing DSA development, selection and accessibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For the last five years, about 6% of Singaporean students admitted via DSA to a secondary school were recipients of MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) or the Full Independent School Bursary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: These are students whose monthly gross household income is $3,000 or less, or whose monthly per capita income is $750 or less.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MOE is reviewing the DSA scheme across three aspects: development, selection and accessibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Development: to ensure that schools focus on providing opportunities that add value to both their DSA and non-DSA students' development, whether in their school programmes, co-curricular activities (CCAs) or academic pursuits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For selection: notwithstanding the need for schools to weigh different considerations when assessing DSA applicants, we want to strengthen the DSA selection process so that it continues to be undergirded by the principles of transparency, objectivity, inclusiveness and student centricity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And accessibility: to ensure that DSA remains accessible and students from all backgrounds are recognised not just for their performance, but also their potential in specific talent areas.

sections.label: DSA merit and development
sections.summary: The Minister agrees student background should be considered but avoids quotas, and says schools must value-add to children's development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we agree with the Member that we should take into account the background of the students in assessing their performance and potential at a point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I would be careful not to go into a system of setting quotas one way or the other, because that might defeat the purpose of DSA and selection based on merit in terms of potential and performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second supplementary question that the Member asked, indeed, that is what I said in respect of refining the DSA to focus on development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have personally given guidance to the MOE staff and schools and they are aware of my views, that when a school wants to build up a team and wants to perform well, they must make sure that they value-add to the development of the children and not just rely on pure selection for the performance of the team.
